item: accent-color: app-wide accent colour picker (presets plus a custom ColorPicker), applied to every tint and Liquid Glass tint, saved in SettingsStore and backups, updating live
currentBehaviour:
Re-verified against /home/user/pixlaudio-ios at origin/main 86a5cce. Changes from the earlier plan are marked [corrected] or [added]. There is no accent setting today. The app's accent is the `primary` role of one fixed scheme pair, and almost every tint already flows from it.

1. Where the accent comes from
- `Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlLibrary/ArtworkTheme/ArtworkTheme.swift:240-245`: `brandSeed = 0xFF6C_4FF5` and `brandPair = schemePair(seed: brandSeed)`. The style defaults to `.default`, which is `.tonalSpot` (`ArtworkTheme.swift:21`). That builds a TonalSpot scheme (`SeedColorSelector.swift:331-342` `SchemeBuilder.pair`; `DynamicScheme.swift:367-374` sets primary chroma 36). Light primary is #5F5791, dark #C8BFFF (I reproduced both).
- `App/DesignSystem/Theme.swift:21-24`: `ThemeColors.brandLight` / `.brandDark` / `.brand(_:)` wrap that pair. The environment entries `appTheme` / `playerTheme` default to `.brandLight` (`Theme.swift:41,44`).
- `App/Stores/ThemeStore.swift:33-43` `colors(for:)`: `let brand = ThemeColors.brand(colorScheme)` (line 35). If `albumPair` is nil, it returns brand for both. Otherwise it switches on `appearance.playerTheme`:
  - `.albumArt` (the default) → app = brand, player = album;
  - `.global` → album for both;
  - `.default` / `.dynamic` → brand for both.
- `ThemeColors.brand` is used only there. `brandLight`/`brandDark`/`brandPair` appear elsewhere only as env defaults and in `AppTests/LaunchConfigurationTests.swift:186-205`. So changing ThemeStore re-themes everything.
- [added] The roles that come from the seed are more than primary:
  - secondary is hue at chroma 16 (SettingsIcon uses `theme.secondary`, `SettingsRows.swift:118`);
  - tertiary is hue+60;
  - neutral and neutralVariant are the hue at chroma 6/8. These are background and surfaceContainer: the settings row glass tint (`SettingsRows.swift:91-93`) and the root background (`RootView.swift:31`).
  - So an accent seed also gives surfaces a faint cast of its hue.

2. What "accent source" means (`docs/parity.md:40`)
- It is the Player Theme row. `AppearanceSettingsSection.swift:43-50` offers Album Art and "System Dynamic".
- Labels: `SettingsStrings.swift:724-725`. The "System Dynamic" catalog value: `App/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings:8122-8130`.
- `PlayerThemePreference` (`SettingsStore.swift:172-179`) notes that `dynamic` has no iOS source and acts like `default`, i.e. the brand violet.
- `PaletteStyleView.swift:1-20` is an unlinked route that says the palette style is fixed.

3. How the accent is applied today
- Root tint: `RootView.swift:28` `let colors = themeStore.colors(for: colorScheme)`; `:50-51` appTheme/playerTheme; `:52` `.tint(colors.app.primary)`.
- Sheets and covers (`:54-65`): the `.sheet` / `.fullScreenCover` modifiers sit outside the `.tint` in the modifier chain. Their closures re-inject appTheme/playerTheme but **not `.tint`**, so presented content falls back to the static asset.
  - Example: `App/Features/Queue/SleepTimerSheet.swift:257` `.glassProminent` with no tint. It is presented both from the router (`RouteDestinations.swift:52`) and nested from `QueueSheet.swift:76`.
  - [added] The lyrics screen and sync editor are covers (`RouteDestinations.swift:70-71`). They apply `.alwaysDarkTheme(themeStore)` (`LyricsView.swift:173`, `LyricsSyncEditorView.swift:81`; defined at `Theme.swift:65-71`), which sets no tint either.
- Static asset: `App/Assets.xcassets/AccentColor.colorset` (#7C5CFF light, #9D8CFF dark, #6140E0 high contrast), wired in `project.yml:62` (`ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME`). It already differs from the in-app primary (#5F5791). UIKit-backed alerts and dialogs use it: there are 36 `.alert(`/`.confirmationDialog(` call sites in App/.
- Liquid Glass tints, all from `theme.primary` / `primaryContainer`:
  - tab bar pill: `GlassNavBar.swift:31-33` → UIKit `LiquidTabBar.swift:87-96` (updateUIView → apply) and `:289-295`; it updates live;
  - sheet tab capsules: `LiquidTabCapsule.swift:36-39`;
  - selected pill: `GlassPillRow.swift:117`;
  - `GlassMenuButtons.swift:37` (the caller's tint);
  - playing SongCard: `SongCard.swift:34`, `:110`;
  - `GlassTint` strengths: `GlassStyle.swift:8-12`.
- Controls: toggles (`SettingsRows.swift:200`), sliders (`:363`), section captions (`:68`). [corrected] There are 47 explicit `.tint(theme.primary)` calls (94 `.tint(` calls in all), not about 60.
- UIKit bridges re-read colours on update: `DevicesSheet.swift:383/388`, `EqualizerView.swift:426/431`, `AirPlayRoutePicker.swift:24-25`. Its `activeTint` defaults to `.accentColor` (line 9), but every caller passes explicit colours (`DevicesSheet.swift:225,234,263`).
- Album-art theming feeds `playerTheme`: mini player `MiniPlayerBar.swift:26`, the full player, and lyrics `LyricsView.swift:48`.
- Detail pages use `ArtworkThemed` (`DetailComponents.swift:215-223`) → `AlbumSchemeReader` (`LibraryPages.swift:296-326`). That falls back to the environment's `appTheme` when there's no art, so it will pick up the accent. With art it stays album-coloured.

4. Settings storage
- `AppearanceSettings` (`SettingsStore.swift:225-287`) holds appThemeMode, playerTheme, paletteStyle and colorAccuracy under Android keys. There are no iOS-only keys yet.
- `PreferenceKeys` is a `nonisolated enum` (`:9-163`).
- Live re-read after a restore: `SettingsReload.swift:28-45` (`sync(...)`), called from `BackupService.swift:285`.

5. Backups
- `SettingsBackup.exportValues` (`SettingsBackup.swift:191-208`) exports only keys where `AndroidPreferenceCatalog.kind(of:) == .portable`.
- [added] `SettingsBackup.kind(of:)` (`:176-179`) already returns `.string` for any portable key missing from `androidTypes`.
- Restores go through `PreferencesModule.plan` (`Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlBackup/Modules/PreferencesModule.swift:238-268`). Unknown keys go to `unknownKeys` and are skipped. The catalogue is at `:102-166`.
- So a new key is neither backed up nor restored unless it is in the catalogue.
- A global-settings restore clears with `.allExcept` (`SettingsBackup.swift:264-270`).
- [added, verified] Android's `importPreferencesFromBackup` writes every entry whatever its key (`UserPreferencesRepository.kt:1561-1590` on `origin/android-int-oct3`). So an iOS-only key survives an iOS → Android → iOS round trip.

6. Android
- `origin/android-int-oct3` `SettingsCategoryScreen.kt` ~lines 644-735 (verified):
  - Global Theme: language, app theme, smooth corners, disable blur, scrollbar.
  - Now Playing: Player Theme (ALBUM_ART / DYNAMIC), file info, a palette link, carousel.
- No accent setting, so this is an owner-requested divergence.

7. Tests and launch arguments
- Appearance shots: `UITests/SettingsScreenshotTests.swift:13-14`. The `capture` helper is at `:68-88`; `ScreenshotTests.capture` is at `:108-133`. Both name attachments `<screen>-<appearance>`.
- UI tests use `SettingsStore.ephemeral()` (`SettingsStore.swift:208-213`; `AppEnvironment.swift:84`).
- `LaunchConfiguration` (`UITestLaunchRouter.swift:254-300`) has no accent flag.
- Swift 6 conventions here: nested types in `nonisolated` enums are explicitly marked `nonisolated` (`SettingsBackup.swift:12,253`; `UITestLaunchRouter.swift:265`). iOS-only strings live in `extension L10n` files (`App/Features/Backup/BackupStrings.swift`, `App/Services/Updates/UpdateNotifier.swift:125`), not in the generated `SettingsStrings.swift` (its header says it's generated from Android and not to hand-edit).

recommendedPlan.change:
In `enum SchemeBuilder` (after `pair`, line ~342) add `static func accentPair(seed: ARGB) -> ColorRolesPair`.
- `let source = Hct.fromInt(seed)`; compute `forceNeutral` exactly as `pair` does (lines 333-334).
- For each isDark: `let base = DynamicScheme.tonalSpot(source, isDark: isDark)`, then `DynamicScheme(source: source, variant: .tonalSpot, isDark: isDark, contrastLevel: 0, primary: .fromHueAndChroma(source.hue, max(36.0, source.chroma)), secondary: base.secondaryPalette, tertiary: base.tertiaryPalette, neutral: base.neutralPalette, neutralVariant: base.neutralVariantPalette).colorRoles()`. The signature matches `DynamicScheme.swift:336-337`.
- If `forceNeutral`, map both through `grayscale`, as `pair` does.
- Result: TonalSpot surfaces and role tones (the same contrast guarantees), but the primary keeps the picked colour's saturation.
- Verified numbers (material-color-utilities 0.3.0 run again in the scratchpad, never shipped):
  - light primaries: Red #BD0E12, Blue #005DB8, Green #006E28, Yellow #705D00, Pink #BE0036, Purple #9026C3, Indigo #4D4AD5, Orange #885200, Mint #006A65; vivid brand violet #5D3CE5.
  - TonalSpot alone: Red #904A42, Blue #405F90.
  - [added] Dark primaries are tone 80 and gamut-limited, so they are pastel and mostly identical to TonalSpot: Red #FFB4AA, Blue #AAC7FF, Green #53E16F (TonalSpot #9ED49D), Yellow #E9C400.
  - Contrast: primary/onPrimary 6.44-7.76:1, primary vs background ≥ 6.12:1 (light) and ≥ 10.86:1 (dark), primaryContainer/onPrimaryContainer ≥ 7.19:1.
  - Graphite #8E8E93 is forced neutral → #6A6A6A light / #D7D7D7 dark; 5.41 / 5.27 / 6.61:1 (light), 8.02 / 12.80 / 6.61:1 (dark).

After line 245 add `/// The app-wide accent (iOS-only, owner request 2026-10-07) ... public static func accentPair(seed: UInt32) -> ColorRolesPair { SchemeBuilder.accentPair(seed: seed) }`. Leave `brandSeed` / `brandPair` unchanged, so the default colours stay the same (but see the RootView step: sheets and alerts change slightly).

For the preset seeds, in light and dark, use `Contrast.ratioOfTones(ColorUtils.lstarFromArgb(a), ColorUtils.lstarFromArgb(b))` (`DynamicScheme.swift:86`, `ColorScience.swift:124`). Tests:
- primary/onPrimary ≥ 4.5;
- primary vs background ≥ 3;
- primaryContainer vs onPrimaryContainer ≥ 4.5. Graphite has the least margin (5.41 / 5.27 / 6.61 light) and still passes.
- 0xFF8E8E93 gives r==g==b for primary.
- `Hct.fromInt(accent.primary).chroma >= Hct.fromInt(tonalSpot.primary).chroma`. Use ≥, not >: dark tones and Mint are equal.
- `background` and `surfaceContainer` equal `ArtworkTheme.schemePair(seed:)`'s.
Record the tests in docs/test-parity.md as iOS-only (no Android counterpart).

- Add `static let iosOnly: [String] = ["accent_color_v1"]`, documented as: settings only the iOS app has, restored by name; Android stores them untouched (`UserPreferencesRepository.importPreferencesFromBackup`).
- In `table` (lines 159-166) add `for k in iosOnly { t[k] = .portable }`.
- Update the enum doc (lines 96-97) to mention the iOS-only list.
- In `Packages/PixlCore/Tests/PixlBackupTests/ModuleTests.swift:123-136`, add `#expect(AndroidPreferenceCatalog.kind(of: "accent_color_v1") == .portable)` and include `AndroidPreferenceCatalog.iosOnly` in the uniqueness `all` list.

- In `PreferenceKeys` (before the closing brace at line 163), add `// iOS-only (owner requests)` and `static let accentColor = "accent_color_v1"`.
- In `AppearanceSettings` (lines 225-287), add `/// Settings › Appearance › Accent color: "#RRGGBB" seed, "" = PixlAudio's violet.` and `var accentColor: String { didSet { defaults.set(accentColor, forKey: PreferenceKeys.accentColor) } }`.
- Initialise it in `init` with `defaults.string(PreferenceKeys.accentColor, default: "")`.
- Store a String (not an Int): an ARGB above Int32.max would flip sign as an Android `int`.
- Update the `PlayerThemePreference` doc (lines 172-173): `dynamic` now means "the accent scheme".
- The `accentSeed` computed property from the earlier plan is optional; ThemeStore can call `AccentPalette.seed(hex:)` directly.

(1) `nonisolated enum AccentPalette` containing:
- `nonisolated struct Preset: Identifiable, Sendable { let id: String; let name: String; let hex: String }`. Nested types must be marked `nonisolated` explicitly, as `SettingsBackup.swift:12,253` does.
- `static let presets`: PixlAudio (""), Blue #0A84FF, Indigo #5E5CE6, Purple #BF5AF2, Pink #FF2D55, Red #FF453A, Orange #FF9F0A, Yellow #FFD60A, Green #34C759, Mint #00C7BE, Graphite #8E8E93. With Custom that makes 12 cells.
- `static func seed(hex: String) -> UInt32?`: trims an optional '#', takes exactly 6 hex digits, returns `0xFF000000 | rgb`; "" or invalid → nil.
- `static func hex(argb: UInt32) -> String`: `String(format: "#%06X", argb & 0xFFFFFF)`.
- `static func hex(_ color: Color) -> String`: `let r = color.resolve(in: EnvironmentValues())`, then clamp `r.red/green/blue` (sRGB Floats, extended range) to 0…1, ×255, round. A fresh `EnvironmentValues()` (iOS 13) avoids `@Environment(\.self)` in the row: that would invalidate it on every environment change, and a ColorPicker colour is static anyway.
- `static let resolved: [String: ColorRolesPair]` (preset id → `ArtworkTheme.brandPair` or `ArtworkTheme.accentPair(seed:)`). Read it from a `Task.detached`; the 22 schemes' cost is unmeasured.
- `static func dynamicPrimary(_ pair: ColorRolesPair) -> UIColor`: precompute `let light = UIColor(Color(argb: pair.light.primary)), dark = UIColor(Color(argb: pair.dark.primary))` and return `UIColor { $0.userInterfaceStyle == .dark ? dark : light }`. UIColor is Sendable. Build the closure in this nonisolated function so it is not inferred `@MainActor` (Swift 6 would add a main-actor check that traps if UIKit resolves the colour off the main thread).

(2) Top-level (NOT nested in AccentPalette, so it keeps the default MainActor isolation) `@MainActor enum WindowTint { static func apply(_ pair: ColorRolesPair) }`. It sets `tintColor = AccentPalette.dynamicPrimary(pair)` on every window of every `UIApplication.shared.connectedScenes` `UIWindowScene`. The app has one scene (`project.yml` `UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes: false`). This lets UIKit-backed alerts, confirmation dialogs, menus and the colour picker follow the accent. Whether it does on iOS 26/27 is unproven (see risks).

(3) Don't name anything `Material…` (`ci/check-forbidden.sh:67`).

- Add `@ObservationIgnored private var accentCache: (hex: String, pair: ColorRolesPair)?`.
- Add `var accentPair: ColorRolesPair`: read `appearance.accentColor` (observed, so every reader re-renders on change); return the cache when the hex matches; otherwise build `AccentPalette.seed(hex:).map(ArtworkTheme.accentPair(seed:)) ?? ArtworkTheme.brandPair` and cache it. One pair is computed once per change on the main thread, the same cost as the lazy `brandPair` today.
- In `colors(for:)` replace line 35 with `let brand = ThemeColors(roles: accentPair.roles(dark: isDark), isDark: isDark)`.
- The `switch appearance.playerTheme` (lines 38-42) stays: Album Art keeps album colours in the player and the accent elsewhere; Global uses album colours everywhere; Dynamic/Default use the accent everywhere.
- Update the header doc (lines 7-8).

- Add `.tint(colors.app.primary)` inside the `.sheet` closure (after line 57) and the `.fullScreenCover` closure (after line 64), so presented content stops falling back to the static AccentColor asset.
- Add `.onChange(of: themeStore.accentPair, initial: true) { _, pair in WindowTint.apply(pair) }` next to the `.task(id:)` at line 66. `ColorRolesPair` is Hashable (`ArtworkTheme.swift:161`).
- No animation on accent change: the root `.animation` (line 53) is keyed to `albumPair` only, so the accent snaps and the three tab stacks aren't composited mid-fade (docs/performance.md).
- [corrected] This step changes the default look a little: glassProminent buttons and default-tinted controls in sheets and covers (e.g. Sleep Timer OK), and alert buttons, move from the asset's #7C5CFF/#9D8CFF to the in-app #5F5791/#C8BFFF. Expect diffs in the PlayerScreenshotTests and BackupOnboardingScreenshotTests sheet and cover shots.

- In `alwaysDarkTheme` (lines 65-71) add `.tint(colors.app.primary)`. It sits inside the cover-level tint, so it wins, and the lyrics screen and sync editor get the dark-tone accent instead of the light one on black.
- Update the doc comments at lines 39-44 and 21-24: "the accent scheme (PixlAudio's violet by default, Settings › Appearance › Accent color)".

`struct AccentColorRow: View` with `let selectedHex: String`, `let onSelect: (String) -> Void`, `@Environment(\.appTheme) theme`.

Layout:
- Like `ThemeSelectorRow` (`SettingsRows.swift:220-273`), but `HStack(alignment: .top)`: `SettingsIcon(systemImage: "paintpalette")` (24 pt) with `.padding(.trailing, 16)`.
- A VStack: title (`.titleMedium`, onSurface), 6 pt, subtitle (`.bodyMedium`, onSurfaceVariant), 12 pt, then the swatch grid.
- `.padding(16)`, `.settingsRowGlass()` (no interactive glass on the row itself).

Grid [corrected]:
- Use a non-lazy `Grid` (or two `HStack` rows) of 6 FLEXIBLE cells with a 44 pt hit target and 34 pt swatch. At 402 pt the text column is 298 pt (402 − 2×16 page − 2×16 row − 24 − 16), but on a 375 pt phone it is only 271 pt, so the fixed 284 pt grid from the earlier plan would overflow.
- Each preset is a Button with `PressScaleButtonStyle()` and a `Circle().fill(...)`: a fill, not glass on glass.
- Selected: `Circle().strokeBorder(theme.onSurface, lineWidth: 2.5)` plus a `checkmark` (13 pt bold) in the swatch's `onPrimary`.
- Swatch colour = the resolved `primary` for `theme.isDark`, from `@State swatches: [String: ColorRolesPair] = [:]` filled by `.task { swatches = await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) { AccentPalette.resolved }.value }`. Fall back to the raw seed until it's ready.

Custom cell [corrected]:
- In `init`, set `_picked = State(initialValue: Color(argb: AccentPalette.seed(hex: selectedHex) ?? ArtworkTheme.brandSeed))` and `_seededHex = State(initialValue: AccentPalette.hex(argb: AccentPalette.seed(hex: selectedHex) ?? ArtworkTheme.brandSeed))`.
- `ColorPicker(selection: $picked, supportsOpacity: false) { Text(L10n.settingsAccentColorCustom) }.labelsHidden()`, with a selection ring when `selectedHex` is not a preset.
- Debounce correctly. `try? await Task.sleep` swallows the cancellation and would commit every drag step:
  `.task(id: picked) { do { try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(180)) } catch { return }; let hex = AccentPalette.hex(picked); if hex != seededHex, hex != selectedHex { onSelect(hex) } }`
- When a preset is tapped, also set `picked` and `seededHex` to that preset's colour, so reopening the picker starts from it and the re-seed is never committed.

Also:
- `.pixlHaptic(.selection, trigger: selectedHex)` (`Haptics.swift:12`).
- Accessibility: `.accessibilityLabel(name)` and `.isSelected`; identifiers `settings.accent.<id>`, `settings.accent.custom`, row `settings.accentColor`.

- In Global Theme, insert `AccentColorRow(selectedHex: appearance.accentColor) { appearance.accentColor = $0 }` right after the App Theme `ThemeSelectorRow` (after line 35). Order becomes: language (hidden), App Theme, Accent color, Disable blur, Show scrollbar.
- If Hoa agrees (owner decision 2), change the Now Playing option at lines 46-47 to label `L10n.settingsPlayerThemeAccent` ("Accent Color"), keeping key `dynamic` for backup compatibility. This needs a NEW key: the catalog's "System Dynamic" (`Localizable.xcstrings:8125-8128`) would override an edited defaultValue.
- Update the header comment (lines 4-10).

`SettingsStrings.swift` is generated from Android (its header says don't hand-edit). Follow `BackupStrings.swift` instead.

In `AppearanceSettings.reload` (lines 28-45) add `sync(\.accentColor, self, f)`, so a restored backup re-tints the app live (ThemeStore observes `accentColor`).

[corrected] No edit is needed. `kind(of:)` (lines 176-179) already returns `.string` for any catalogue-portable key missing from `androidTypes`, so `accent_color_v1` exports as a string once the PreferencesModule step lands. risks: [corrected] Dark mode stays pastel. With the vivid variant, light-mode primaries are vivid, but dark-mode primaries are tone 80 and gamut-limited, so they're nearly the same as TonalSpot: red → #FFB4AA (salmon), blue → #AAC7FF, Pink #FFB3B5. Hoa may expect an iOS-style saturated #FF453A in dark mode. Only option C (exact colour) gives that. Put this plainly in owner decision 1.

ColorPicker updates its binding continuously while the system picker is dragged. Each commit recolours the whole app and builds a scheme pair. Debounce with `do { try await Task.sleep } catch { return }`: the earlier plan's `try?` swallowed the cancellation and committed every step. Also never commit the seeded value; otherwise opening the page would save #6C4FF5 over the default "".

System alerts and the window tint:
- The forum thread cited earlier (hackingwithswift 7193) shows SwiftUI `.accentColor`/`.tint` not reaching `Alert`. Its workaround is `UIView.appearance(whenContainedInInstancesOf: [UIAlertController.self]).tintColor`, NOT the window tint. It also warns this depends on SwiftUI using UIAlertController internally.
- Setting `UIWindow.tintColor` is standard UIKit inheritance (`UIView.tintColor` docs), but whether iOS 26/27's glass alerts and dialogs show it is unverified.
- Check on Hoa's phone; fall back to the UIAppearance line if needed.
- Until then the static `AccentColor` asset can still show #7C5CFF in places (the launch screen, any system UI that ignores the window tint).

Default look changes slightly. Adding `.tint` to the sheet/cover closures and the window moves default-tinted controls in sheets/covers, and alert buttons, from the asset's #7C5CFF/#9D8CFF to the in-app #5F5791/#C8BFFF, even with no accent chosen. It's more consistent, but it's a visible change. The earlier claim of "no screenshot churn for the default" was wrong for sheet/cover shots.

Surfaces and icons shift hue with the accent. The neutral palettes (chroma 6/8) and secondary (chroma 16) follow the seed hue. So the settings row glass tint (`theme.surfaceContainer`), the root background and SettingsIcon (`theme.secondary`) take a faint cast of the accent. This is how Material dynamic colour behaves and arguably what 'app-wide' means, but rows don't look 'as now' for non-violet accents.

Restoring an Android backup's global settings uses `.allExcept` clearing (`SettingsBackup.swift:264-270`), which removes every portable key. ownerDecisions:
How close should the app's accent stay to the colour you pick?
(a) Vivid (recommended). In light mode it keeps your colour's punch: red stays a real red (#BD0E12), blue a strong blue (#005DB8). In dark mode, like today's violet, it becomes a light pastel (red #FFB4AA, blue #AAC7FF), so the dark text and icons on it stay readable.
(b) Soft: the same muted style today's violet uses (red becomes brick #904A42 in light mode).
(c) Exact: your exact colour everywhere, including a saturated iOS-style dark mode, with black or white text picked automatically. Bright yellow or very light picks can then be hard to see on light backgrounds.

Should the accent also colour the player and mini player?
(a) Recommended: no. Keep album-art colours there as now, and rename the unused 'System Dynamic' Player Theme option to 'Accent Color', so you can switch the player to your accent whenever you want.
(b) Always use the accent in the player too (album colours off).
Should the default stay today's soft PixlAudio violet (no change for anyone who doesn't pick a colour), or become the vivid violet (#5D3CE5) to match the other presets?

Presets: Blue, Indigo, Purple, Pink, Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Mint, Graphite and Custom. Graphite as built is a neutral grey; do you want it grey, or true black-and-white? Keep this set, or name the colours you want?

  - `Color.resolve(in:)`, iOS 17: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/color/resolve(in:)
  - `Color.Resolved`, iOS 17, "stored in the Linear sRGB color space, using extended range": https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/color/resolved
    - `red` (Float) is "the amount of red in the color in the sRGB color space": https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/color/resolved/red
    - `linearRed` is the linear one: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/color/resolved/linearred
  - `EnvironmentValues.init()`, iOS 13: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/environmentvalues/init()
  - `View.tint(_:)`, iOS 15 (`nonisolated`), "Use this method to override the default accent color for this view… the tint color is always respected": https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/tint(_:)
  - `View.onChange(of:initial:_:)` with V: Equatable, iOS 17: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/onchange(of:initial:_:)-4psgg
  - `UIView.tintColor`, iOS 7, "the first nondefault tint color value in the view's hierarchy, ascending from… the view itself": https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiview/tintcolor
  - `UIColor(dynamicProvider:)`, iOS 13, declared as `@escaping (UITraitCollection) -> UIColor`: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uicolor/init(dynamicprovider:)
  - UIColor conforms to Sendable: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uicolor
  - `UIWindowScene.windows`, iOS 13: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiwindowscene/windows
  - HIG Color (verified quote): "the system applies the app accent color to the background in prominent buttons… Refrain from adding color to the background of multiple controls". It also says to supply light, dark and increased-contrast variants for custom colours: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color
- [corrected] Forum thread https://www.hackingwithswift.com/forums/swiftui/alert-button-color-conforming-to-accentcolor/7193:
  - It confirms `.accentColor` doesn't change SwiftUI Alert buttons.
  - Its workaround is `UIView.appearance(whenContainedInInstancesOf: [UIAlertController.self]).tintColor`, with the caveat that it relies on SwiftUI using UIAlertController.
  - It does not show the window tint working. That is standard UIKit inheritance, unverified for iOS 26/27 glass alerts.
- Colour maths: I re-ran Google's material-color-utilities 0.3.0 (npm, scratchpad only, never shipped). It's the same algorithm PixlLibrary ports (`DynamicScheme.swift` header: material 1.14.0 / upstream 03336bf6de). Seed-chroma primary versus TonalSpot and Vibrant:
  - light, accent / tonalSpot / vibrant: Blue #005DB8 / #405F90 / #005DB8; Red #BD0E12 / #904A42 / #C0000D; Indigo #4D4AD5 / #595992 / #4338FF; Purple #9026C3 / #755085 / #9600D4; Green #006E28 / #38693C / #006E28; Yellow #705D00 / #6F5D0E / #705D00; Mint #006A65 (all three); brand #5D3CE5 / #5F5791 / #5B2CFF.
  - dark: mostly the same as TonalSpot (Blue #AAC7FF, Red #FFB4AA, brand #C8BFFF).
  - Contrast: primary/onPrimary 6.44-7.76:1; primary vs background ≥ 6.12:1 (light) and ≥ 10.86:1 (dark); containers ≥ 7.19:1.
  - Graphite (forced neutral): #6A6A6A / #D7D7D7, with 5.41:1 primary/onPrimary in light.
  - Contrast is guaranteed by the fixed role tones (`DynamicScheme.swift:560-575` primary 40/80 with contrast curve 3.0 against background), not by the hue.

options.name: A. Seed-chroma accent scheme (recommended)
options.description: New `ArtworkTheme.accentPair(seed:)`: TonalSpot palettes and role tones, with the primary palette at the seed's own chroma (min 36). ThemeStore swaps it in for `brandPair`. The default ("") keeps the current `brandPair`.
options.pros: Vivid light-mode accents with contrast guaranteed in light and dark; respects a muted custom pick, unlike Vibrant; calm TonalSpot surfaces (chroma 6), lightly tinted by the accent hue; about 15 lines of PixlLibrary code using the existing ported maths; default colours unchanged.
options.cons: Not the exact picked colour: brightness is set per mode (yellow becomes dark gold in light mode), and dark mode stays pastel (tone 80).

options.name: B. Plain TonalSpot of the seed
options.description: Use the existing `ArtworkTheme.schemePair(seed:)` as-is, the same algorithm as today's violet.
options.pros: Zero new maths; consistent with the current brand look.
options.cons: Heavily mutes saturated picks in light mode (red → brick #904A42, blue → slate #405F90). Likely to read as 'it didn't use my colour'.

options.name: C. Exact colour override
options.description: Keep the scheme from the seed, but set `primary` to the exact picked colour in both modes. `onPrimary` is black or white by WCAG contrast; optionally shift the tone when contrast vs background is below 3:1.
options.pros: What you pick is exactly what you see; the only option with an iOS-like saturated dark mode.
options.cons: Needs new contrast and tone-shifting code and tests; light or very bright picks can hurt legibility; `primaryContainer`/`inversePrimary` no longer match `primary`.

options.name: D. Existing Vibrant variant [added]
options.description: `ArtworkTheme.schemePair(seed:style: .vibrant)`, already ported (`DynamicScheme.swift:376-385`: primary chroma 200, rotated secondary/tertiary hues, neutral chroma 10/12).
options.pros: Zero new maths; presets come out about as vivid as option A (Blue #005DB8, Red #C0000D).
options.cons: It ignores the pick's own saturation: a dusty custom colour gets maxed out. Its rotated secondary/tertiary hues and stronger surface tint (chroma 10 vs 6) change the look of every settings row and card more than option A.
